name: Proto-Polynesian
notes: Inventory: Table 2.1 (p. 22) and §3.1 (p. 73). Tongic and Nuclear Polynesian are the primary split (p. 25; Figure 1.2, p. 3). Entered directly under POc: Proto-Central Pacific is held back (decision ppn-parent). Marck doubts the PPn *s/*h distinction (Table 2.2 note 5, p. 24) but keeps it, as does Wilson (2021: 44).

name: Proto-Tongic
notes: Tongan and Niuean (Figure 1.2, p. 3). PPn *s and *h fell together as *h and *r was lost (p. 25).
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Nuclear Polynesian
notes: All Polynesian languages other than Tongic (p. 118). PPn *r merged with *l and *h was lost (p. 25). East Uvean, East Futunan, Pukapukan and the 'Futunic' Outliers are unclassified Nuclear Polynesian (§5.5, p. 128).
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Ellicean
notes: Samoan, Ellicean Outlier and East Polynesian (§5.6, p. 129; Figure 1.2, p. 3); defined by three sporadic vowel changes and no consonant change (p. 129); first proposed on the evidence of pronominal systems. Glottolog's Ellicean (elli1239) is Pukapuka, Samoan-Tokelauan and Tuvalu, a different group, so no glottocode. Wilson (2021: 43) no longer accepts the group.
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Ellicean Outlier
notes: Tuvalu, Tokelauan and the Central and Northern Outliers, as in Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24). Marck calls the evidence for the group weak: one shared sporadic vowel change (§5.7, pp. 129-130). Tokelauan shares sporadic changes with Samoan (§5.8, pp. 130-131; decision tok-placement).
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-East Polynesian
notes: Continues the Nuclear Polynesian consonants with one phonetic change, *l > *r (p. 25). The first split is between Rapanui and Central East Polynesian (p. 25). Wilson (2021) places it under Proto-Central Northern Outlier-East Polynesian and divides it into Distal and Proximal dialects.
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Central East Polynesian
notes: Lost *q and merged *f with *s or *w in certain environments (p. 25). Walworth (2014: 268) keeps the group but puts all its languages directly under it; Wilson (2021: 43) does not accept it.
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Marquesic
notes: Hawaiian and Nuclear Marquesic (Figure 1.2, p. 3). No regular consonant change, with the possible phonetic exception of *s > *h (p. 25). Not accepted by Walworth (2014: 267-268) or Wilson (2021: 43).
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Nuclear Marquesic
notes: Marquesan and Mangarevan, defined by a diffused assimilation of low vowels (§3.3.1, p. 79; §5.12, p. 133).
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Tahitic
notes: Tahitian, Māori, Tuamotuan, Rarotongan, Mangaia, Penrhyn, Manihiki (Figure 1.2, p. 3) and the other Tahitic lects of Table 2.2. No regular consonant or vowel change from PCE (p. 25; Table 3.1 note 21). Wilson (2021: 38) equates it with his PEPNP(S); Glottolog's Southern East Polynesian Proximal (sout3383) has the same members. Walworth (2014: 268) does not accept it.
inherit_note: Unchanged: Marck's Table 2.2 (pp. 23-24) gives the same consonant, and Table 3.1 (p. 74) no regular vowel change.

name: Proto-Southeast Solomons Outlier-East Polynesian

inherit_note: Wilson (2021) gives no phonological change for this node; its inventory is taken as that of PNPN.

name: Proto-East Polynesian Distal

inherit_note: Wilson (2021: 44) assumes one phoneme inventory for PNPN, PCNO-EPN, PEPN, PEPND, PFEPN, PEPNP and its subdialects.

name: Proto-East Polynesian Proximal
